rst31-v2-r2-found-a-statistics.title: Do not move percentages into a different explanation
rst31-v2-r2-found-a-statistics.text: The text revised in 2021 mentions at least 90% in its food-poisoning classification explanation and 80% in a passage about employees and norovirus. Do not assume a common population or substitute these for current rates of all food poisoning. Do not invent unverified survey years, subjects, denominators or definitions. Understand preventive actions; when current rates are needed, check the conditions of that survey.

rst31-v2-r2-found-q001.objective: Keep historical percentages within their context.
rst31-v2-r2-found-q001.stem: An old text mentions at least 90% and 80% in separate explanations. How should training materials handle them?
options: Guess and add missing survey years or denominators
Check each context and survey conditions, leave unverified information unguessed, and do not declare current rates
Compare them as figures from the same population
Use 80% as the current employee-related share of all food poisoning
rst31-v2-r2-found-q001.explanation: Do not mix percentages from different contexts. State limits when timing, subjects or denominators are unverified; do not generalize to the current whole.
reasons: Do not add guessed information as fact
It preserves contextual limits without turning unknowns into facts
A common population has not been verified
It extends an old context to all current food poisoning
